jurisdiction.name: International Telecommunication Union
jurisdiction.overview: Official documents of this organisation are listed on its own page and are not counted in member countries' totals.

narrative.summary: ITU's Member States have adopted resolutions directing the Union's work on artificial intelligence at each of its main conferences: the Plenipotentiary Conference (Bucharest, 2022), the World Telecommunication Standardization Assembly (New Delhi, 2024) and the World Telecommunication Development Conference (Baku, 2025). These set ITU's mandate on AI standardization, capacity-building and support to developing countries; ITU also co-leads UN inter-agency work on AI and hosts the AI for Good platform. ITU also published the 2025 Joint Statement on Artificial Intelligence and the Rights of the Child, issued with the UN Committee on the Rights of the Child, UNICEF and other UN bodies.

instruments.official_title: Resolution 214 (Bucharest, 2022) - Artificial intelligence technologies and telecommunications/information and communication technologies
instruments.english_title: Artificial intelligence technologies and telecommunications/information and communication technologies
instruments.summary: Plenipotentiary Conference resolution directing ITU to continue studying, sharing information on and building capacity for AI in telecommunications/ICTs, and to foster an ICT ecosystem that supports AI deployment. It instructs the Secretary-General to coordinate this work, cooperate with other UN agencies including through AI for Good, share knowledge especially with developing countries, and report annually to the ITU Council and to the next Plenipotentiary Conference.
instruments.current_status: Resolution 214 adopted by the ITU Plenipotentiary Conference (Bucharest, 2022), as printed in the 2023 collection of ITU basic texts.

instruments.official_title: Resolution 101 (New Delhi, 2024) - Standardization activities of the ITU Telecommunication Standardization Sector on artificial intelligence technologies in support of telecommunications/information and communication technologies
instruments.english_title: Standardization activities of the ITU Telecommunication Standardization Sector on artificial intelligence technologies in support of telecommunications/ICTs
instruments.summary: Directs ITU-T study groups to keep applying AI to telecommunications/ICTs in developing Recommendations, guidelines and best practices and to review and update AI-related Recommendations. Tasks the Director of the Telecommunication Standardization Bureau with sharing information on ITU-T's AI work, especially with developing countries, supporting the AI for Good platform and providing technical guidance on implementing AI standards. Invites Member States and other members to promote adoption of these Recommendations.
instruments.current_status: Resolution 101 adopted by the World Telecommunication Standardization Assembly (New Delhi, 15-24 October 2024); it recalls UNGA resolutions 78/265 and 78/311.

instruments.english_title: Joint Statement on Artificial Intelligence and the Rights of the Child
instruments.issuing_authority: ITU, UN Committee on the Rights of the Child, UNICEF, ILO, IPU, UNESCO, UNICRI, UNODA, OHCHR, Special Representatives of the UN Secretary-General for Children and Armed Conflict and on Violence against Children, UN Special Rapporteur on the sale, sexual exploitation and sexual abuse of children, and Safe Online (published by ITU)
instruments.publisher_name: ITU, UN Committee on the Rights of the Child, UNICEF, ILO, IPU, UNESCO, UNICRI, UNODA, OHCHR, Special Representatives of the UN Secretary-General for Children and Armed Conflict and on Violence against Children, UN Special Rapporteur on the sale, sexual exploitation and sexual abuse of children, and Safe Online (published by ITU)
instruments.summary: Joint statement by UN treaty bodies, agencies and mandate-holders together with the Inter-Parliamentary Union and Safe Online, setting out a child rights-based approach to AI. It addresses child rights-based AI governance by States and by UN and regional organizations, responsibility, accountability and transparency, child safety, data protection and privacy, the best interests of the child, non-discrimination, child participation, environment, capacity building and education.
instruments.current_status: Published by ITU in Geneva, dated November 2025 (ITU publication D-STR-CYB_JOINT-2025, in six UN languages); co-branded by more than 50 further organizations. UNICEF's Knowledge Exchange lists the same statement with an update of 20 March 2026.

leads.title: WTSA Resolution 105 (New Delhi, 2024) - Promoting and strengthening metaverse standardization
ITU-T Recommendations on AI/machine learning (e.g. Y.3172 ML architecture and Y-series ML specifications; F.748.x AI series)
leads.note: Technical standards rather than governance/trustworthiness texts; not enumerated. Add only if a recommendation specifically on AI trustworthiness or governance is identified. Update 2026-11-08: ITU-T F.748.46 (03/2025) Requirements and evaluation methods of artificial intelligence agents based on large scale pre-trained models (https://www.itu.int/rec/T-REC-F.748.46-202503-I/en): Read: approved 2025-03-16, in force, free PDF. Technical standard on evaluating LLM-based AI agents; closest ITU-T text to generative-AI assurance. Related: Y.3062 (02/2025, approved 2025-02-22, SG13) 'Trustworthiness evaluation for IMT-2020 and beyond with autonomous network functions' (network trustworthiness, AI-adjacent). Both remain technical standards per the existing ITU lead policy; record only if the radar decides to include ITU-T AI evaluation standards.
